surfaces.part: teal band with white oval emblem

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a constant 10px wide from row 1 to 29, with only row 0 slightly narrower (8) as a corner trim. There is no widening and narrowing, so no elliptical cap and no overhang. The stacked segments (white sign 1-6, teal band 8-10, yellow number panel 11-18, grey base 20-28) are separated by dark 1-row outlines at rows 7 and 19. Each segment is a face-on vertical panel with no front-edge line, eave shadow, or visible horizontal surface. The top is a flat band at the head, like the red 'column: flat band cap' reference, so the object reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a slim pole-style sign: a light grey/white body, a dark top cap and base, and an orange panel with a '2'. It reads cleanly and is tall and thin, so sparseness alone is not held against it. Measured facts are in line with the references: 12 visible tones per tile (equal to kiosk-a, above bus-shelter-a at 6, below vending-a at 20), 13% near-flat coverage (a little above bus-shelter-a at 9%, well above the 0% of kiosk-a and vending-a), and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are tinted rather than black. Shading is shallow by eye: the pole body has about 3-4 tones with a simple left-light, right-dark split, and the orange panel is nearly flat apart from the numeral. It lacks the grain, per-part highlights and small details that kiosk-a and vending-a carry (awning stripes, windows, buttons). Judged against the whole set it looks thinner and flatter than the richer references and closer to the simple bus-shelter, so I rate density slightly lower. When in doubt, fail.
